note: Eval set for the visual-explanation skill. Case 2 covers the no-preview fallback (browser open + clickable path). Case 3 is the negative case: product code stays untouched.

evals.prompt: Explain how the login flow works in this repo with a visual explanation.
evals.expected_output: A complete self-contained HTML file is written to the workspace, the built file is verified (valid HTML, no broken references, no console errors, no clipping), and the user gets a short message with the source file name plus either a Preview tab or a clickable file path.
assertions: A single self-contained HTML file is produced under the thread workspace
The HTML uses inline CSS, JavaScript, SVG, or canvas with no build step
The file is verified before delivery and anything broken is fixed
Product code is not modified to build the explanation
The closing message names the source file

evals.prompt: Explain the checkout state machine. Note: no preview tools are available in this environment.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not call register_preview or any preview_snapshot/screenshot/logs tool. It verifies the file, opens it in the browser via the terminal, and replies with a clickable absolute file path plus the source file name.
assertions: No preview tool is called when preview tools are unavailable
The file is opened in the browser via a terminal command
The reply contains a clickable absolute file path
The reply names the source file
The built file is verified before delivery

evals.prompt: Explain the caching bug and fix the cache while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: The skill delivers the visual explanation only. Any product-code fix is left to the operator or another skill; the explanation task itself changes no product files.
assertions: The explanation HTML is produced and delivered
No product-code files are modified as part of the explanation
The reply does not claim product code was changed
